prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Greenvale Metro Communications-Based Train Control System: underground/surface; peak/off-peak/engineering. Degradation: stationary/controlled-speed pending separation; cybersecurity/trusted-communications prerequisite. Line Traffic Controller confirms restrictions, independently/verbal-confirms positions; Signal Maintenance Engineer verifies points/vacancy/protection before manual routes; both concur availability/occupancy-changing resets. Automatic return requires stable communications, verified routes/positions, recorded maintenance→operations handback, explicit controller departure-restoration. Metro Operations Control System (Lantern), nonvital: sends Crew Login Token Bundle; displays restrictions without obscuring alarms; excludes maintenance commands. Voice Dispatch Console authorizes restricted-manual unless formal contingency; voice never replaces safety validation/locking. Revenue Train Operator reports hazards, controls speed/stopping/doors; reads back limits/speed/stopping/platform-clear instructions; sends Test Train Clearance Memo after proving-run. North District Zone Controller (Marble)/South District Zone Controller (Orchid): boundary/overlap/receiver-validation; restrictive evidence governs. North validates Temporary Speed Restriction Notice against degraded-map; South inhibits automatic routes in manually-confirmed-occupancy blocks. East Junction Interlocking (Falcon)/West Junction Interlocking prove points/overlaps/flanks/releases. East locks points until field/verified-diagnostic safe-release; sends Axle Counter Reset Request, forbidden under route/approach-locking; engineer uses request after occupancy-checks. West rejects manual-protection conflicts; sends Route Release Exception List to controller. Axle counters independently prove availability; Maple unidentified, records clearance. Platform Screen Door Controller produces Platform Door Status Snapshot; berth/doors constrain departure, not route-proof; protected-local if stopping-accuracy unverified. Atlas Onboard Controller (Kestrel): authenticated activation; initialization/protected-manual/automatic/fallback/cutout; validates authority/context/token, rejects stale acknowledgements, enforces profiles; produces Brake Curve Checksum Log. Dual Channel Odometer supplies distance/speed/confidence; disagreement increases uncertainty/separation. Train Radio Modem sends Radio Handover Audit File; reports failures; retains validated-authority. Wayside Radio Access Network (Saffron): reduce-throughput before extended-manual. Safety Data Communication Network separates safety/nonvital. Cryptographic Key Management Appliance tracks keys/certificates/clocks; produces Encryption Certificate Renewal Pack; bypass only approved-emergency. Cyber Security Officer reviews authentication/lockout/access anomalies. Service Timetable Server supplies approved/controller-verified context; Passenger Information Gateway receives reconciliation, issues

New part:
S202: The Cyber Security Officer shall maintain continuous monitoring of security events from the Safety Data Communication Network, the Wayside Radio Access Network, and the Metro Operations Control System.
S203: Security monitoring shall correlate authentication failures, session resets, rejected messages, configuration changes, and abnormal timing patterns without altering any safety command path.
S204: Alerts affecting train control availability shall be classified using operational impact, affected territory, and whether the event could change train movement authority.
S205: The Line Traffic Controller shall be notified when a cybersecurity event requires a restriction on automatic operation or a change in communications mode.
S206: The Cyber Security Officer uses the audit file to investigate radio session continuity and to confirm that security monitoring records are complete.
S207: The Cryptographic Key Management Appliance shall be the controlled source for operational certificates used by trainborne, wayside, control center, and maintenance components.
S208: Certificate issuance shall require approved asset identity, recorded software baseline, assigned operating domain, and confirmation that the requesting component is authorized for service.
S209: Certificate renewal shall be planned before expiry so that the Atlas Onboard Controller, Train Radio Modem, North District Zone Controller, South District Zone Controller, and West Junction Interlocking do not enter service with degraded trust.
S210: Falcon shall reject any control message with an invalid signature, an expired certificate, or a sequence value outside the accepted window.
S211: Revocation shall be available for a compromised device, a retired device, or a device whose maintenance history can no longer be reconciled with approved configuration records.
S212: The Maintenance Diagnostic Server shall not be used to bypass certificate checks or to create alternate trust paths into safety-related communications.
S213: Administrative access to the Cryptographic Key Management Appliance shall require named accounts, multifactor authentication, separation of duties, and recorded approval for privileged changes.
S214: The Signal Maintenance Engineer may request access needed for fault isolation, but the Cyber Security Officer shall approve security-sensitive permissions before they are enabled.
S215: The Revenue Train Operator shall not be assigned cybersecurity administration duties during passenger service, although security warnings presented in the cab shall remain part of normal operating awareness.
S216: The Metro Operations Control System uses the Test Train Clearance Memo as a controlled prerequisite before accepting security exceptions for non-revenue movement in protected territory.
S217: Audit evidence shall include time-synchronized event records, access approvals, certificate actions, configuration changes, alarm acknowledgements, and operator instructions related to communications security.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
